# Clawd Wars

> A native macOS app (Swift + AppKit, no dependencies) that shows running Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Qwen Code, Gemini CLI and GitHub Copilot CLI sessions as pixel-art Star Wars characters on the desktop or in a window. Every session and subagent is a hero or a villain (one shared cast; with two AIs running they take opposite sides); they fight while they work. Status comes from Claude Code, Codex and Qwen Code hooks (same hook binary, `--assistant codex|qwen|gemini|copilot` and `--event <name>`; per-AI config in `HookInstaller.OtherAI`, payloads translated by `StatusStore.normalize`). Every sprite, effect, location and the app icon are drawn in code — there are no image assets.

## Build and run

- `./build.sh` compiles with `swiftc` (no Xcode project, no SwiftPM), signs, installs `~/Applications/Clawd Wars.app`, merges the hooks into `~/.claude/settings.json` and launches it. `./build.sh --no-hooks` skips the hooks.
- `./release.sh <version>` builds a universal (arm64 + x86_64) release zip, publishes it as a GitHub release and updates the Homebrew cask in `rodclemen/homebrew-tap`.
- There are no unit tests; `<app binary> --chaos=90` is a randomized soak test of the layout (characters on screen, nobody stuck walking, nobody missing, labels on screen and not overlapping) that prints a report and exits non-zero on violations. Check visuals with the frame dump: `CLAWD_SHOT=/tmp/shot.png <app binary> --playground=0,1 --agents=0,1 [--mood=idle]` writes the rendered scene every 5 s (`defaults write <domain> windowMode -bool true` for window mode). `CLAWD_HOVER=<actor key>` fakes a hover; `VADER_DEBUG=1` logs layout and fight roles.
- `Tools/RenderDocs` renders `docs/roster.png`, `docs/locations.png` and `docs/social-preview.png`; `Tools/MakeIcon` renders `Resources/AppIcon.png`.

## Code map

- [Sources/Shared/StatusStore.swift](Sources/Shared/StatusStore.swift): the state shared by hook and app (`~/.claude/vader-status/state.json`, written under `flock`). Turns hook events into session/agent records, assigns villains (random, Vader and Kylo never back to back) and heroes, and builds `SessionSnapshot`s.
- [Sources/Shared/Processes.swift](Sources/Shared/Processes.swift): finds `claude`, `codex`, `qwen`, `gemini` and `copilot` processes, their cwd, start time and CPU time (sessions without hooks, dead-session pruning, "busy" detection).
- [Sources/Hook/main.swift](Sources/Hook/main.swift): the `vader-hook` binary Claude Code runs; reads hook JSON from stdin, never prints, always exits 0.
- [Sources/App/Overlay.swift](Sources/App/Overlay.swift): `OverlayController` — refresh loop, status debounce, fight pairing and formation layout, walking, labels, bubbles, hover cards, menus, window-mode glue, frame dump. `OverlayView.render` draws a list of `DrawItem`s (screen coordinates).
- [Sources/App/Characters.swift](Sources/App/Characters.swift): the shared Clawd body, saber choreography (`kataPose`, `duelPose`), blasters, and all heroes (`Companion`).
- [Sources/App/Leaders.swift](Sources/App/Leaders.swift): all villains (`Leader`), weapons, `FightRole`s, fight effects (`drawFightFX`, `Fighter`), speech bubbles.
- [Sources/App/Locations.swift](Sources/App/Locations.swift) and [Sources/App/Cantina.swift](Sources/App/Cantina.swift): window-mode scenes (`Location`), static layer + animated layer, plus drawing helpers.
- [Sources/App/WindowMode.swift](Sources/App/WindowMode.swift): the window (themed header, scene strip, per-Claude cards, auto height).
- [Sources/App/Jump.swift](Sources/App/Jump.swift): click-to-jump to a session's terminal tab or editor window (AppleScript for Terminal/iTerm2, Accessibility API for VS Code/Cursor incl. native tabs).
- Hook health: `OverlayController.refreshStatus` lists `hookIssues` for AIs that are installed (`HookInstaller.claudeAvailable` / `available`) but not hooked up, or whose sessions ran a turn without reporting (`SessionSnapshot.hookSilent`, e.g. Codex hooks not approved in `/hooks`). These feed the banner, ⚠︎ menu items and a one-per-session notification.
- [Sources/App/HookInstaller.swift](Sources/App/HookInstaller.swift), [Sources/App/Accents.swift](Sources/App/Accents.swift), [Sources/App/Pixel.swift](Sources/App/Pixel.swift) (the `PixelCanvas` all art is drawn on).

## Conventions

- Sprites are 72×52 canvases facing right; the body is x 18…37, y 26…37, feet end at row 43, the hand pivot is (41.5, 34.5). Characters facing left are mirrored by the renderer. `C(0xRRGGBB)` makes a colour; `canvas.pattern(x, y, rows, palette)` draws string art.
- Adding a villain: a case in `Leader` (name, weapon, headTop, optional muzzle), a `draw…` costume, a home in `Location.home(of:)`, a Playground weapon label in `Overlay.swift`, and bump `StatusStore.leaderCount`. Heroes likewise with `Companion` and `companionCount`.
- Cast ids: villains are `Leader.rawValue` (< 100), heroes `100 + Companion.rawValue`; `Cast` (Sources/App/Cast.swift) wraps both and draws either as a session or an agent. Side rules live in `StatusStore.side(for:in:)`, `nextLeader` and `nextAgentCast`.
- Per-AI look lives in `AIStyle` (Sources/App/Accents.swift): outline colour (never dark) and list order. `Actor.assistant` carries it to sprites; cards and the menu group by it.
- Fight rules: Claudes fight Claudes, agents fight agents, a leftover Claude and agent fight each other, anyone else left over cheers; unarmed characters are bystanders.
- Commits follow Conventional Commits; every change gets a CHANGELOG entry.
